answers.explanation: A connection is identified by both ends' address and port, so a web server on 443 and a database on 5432 can share one machine.
The handshake costs one round trip before any data flows.
TCP's ACKs are cumulative: the number of the next byte the receiver is waiting for.
The sender resends when an ACK doesn't come back in time, even if the original actually arrived.
It's the price of a single ordered stream. QUIC avoids it by retransmitting per stream.
When late data is useless, retransmission just adds delay.
QUIC does its own retransmission on top of UDP, per stream, so one lost packet doesn't block unrelated streams.
TCP only hides most failures. If the other side vanishes, TCP eventually gives up and your application sees a timeout.
Flow and congestion control limit bytes in flight. The window grows while things go well and shrinks sharply on loss.
